Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations :

A. 60 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 40 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

B. 55 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 45 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

C. 75 mL $${M \over {5}}$$ HCl + 25 mL $${M \over {5}}$$ NaOH

D. 100 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 100 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
en.explanation:
(A) 60 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 40 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

Mili. moles of HCl = 60 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 6

Mili. moles of NaOH = 40 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 4

Mili. moles of HCl remaining = 6 - 4 = 2

Total volume will be 60 + 40 = 100 mL

Concentration of [H+] = $${{2} \over {100}}$$ = 2 $$ \times $$ 10-2

$$ \therefore $$ pH = 2 - log2 = 1.7

(B) 55 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 45 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

Mili. moles of HCl = 55 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 5.5

Mili. moles of NaOH = 45 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 4.5

Mili. moles of HCl remaining = 5.5 - 4.5 = 1

Concentration of [H+] = $${{1} \over {100}}$$ = 10-2

$$ \therefore $$ pH = 2

(C) 75 mL $${M \over {5}}$$ HCl + 25 mL $${M \over {5}}$$ NaOH

Mili. moles of HCl = 75 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {5}}$$ = 15

Mili. moles of NaOH = 25 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {5}}$$ = 5

Mili. moles of HCl remaining = 15 - 5 = 10

Total volume will be 75 + 25 = 100 mL

Concentration of [H+] = $${{10} \over {100}}$$ = 10-1

$$ \therefore $$ pH = 1

(D) 100 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ HCl + 100 mL $${M \over {10}}$$ NaOH

Mili. moles of HCl = 100 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 10

Mili. moles of NaOH = 100 $$ \times $$ $${1 \over {10}}$$ = 10

Mili. moles of HCl remaining = 10 - 10 = 0

So, it is neutral solution.

$$ \therefore $$ pH = 7

Rseries = nR

In parallel grouping equivalent resistance

Current drawn from a battery when n resistors are connected in series is

Current drawn from same battery when n resistors are connected in parallel is

Given, Initial velocity v = v0 $$\widehat i$$

Electric field E = – E0$$\widehat i$$

$$ \therefore $$Initial de-Brogile wavelength,

$$\lambda $$0 = $${h \over {m{v_0}}}$$

Now force due to electric field on electrons,

$$\overrightarrow F = \left( { - e} \right)\left( { - {E_0}\widehat i} \right) = e{E_0}\widehat i$$

Acceleration produced in the electron,

$$\overrightarrow a = {{\overrightarrow F } \over m} = {{e{E_0}} \over m}\widehat i$$

Now, velocity of electron after time t,

$$\overrightarrow {{v_t}} = \overrightarrow v + \overrightarrow a t$$ = $$\left( {{v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}} \right)\widehat i$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\left| {\overrightarrow {{v_t}} } \right| = {v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}$$

Now, $$\lambda $$t = $${h \over {m{v_t}}}$$

= $${h \over {m\left( {{v_0} + {{e{E_0}t} \over m}} \right)}}$$

= $${h \over {m{v_0}\left( {1 + {{e{E_0}t} \over {m{v_0}}}} \right)}}$$

$$\left( {{F \over {AY}}} \right)l$$ = $$\left( {{{F'} \over {3AY}}} \right){l \over 3}$$

en.explanation:
Force experienced by a charged particle in an electric field, F = qE

As F = ma

$$ \therefore $$ ma = qE

$$ \Rightarrow $$ a = $${{qE} \over m}$$

As electron and proton both fall from same height at rest. Then initial velocity = 0

From the formula, s = ut + $${1 \over 2}a{t^2}$$

$$ \therefore $$ h = $${1 \over 2}a{t^2}$$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ h = $${1 \over 2}{{qE} \over m}{t^2}$$

$$ \therefore $$ t = $$\sqrt {{{2hm} \over {qE}}} $$

$$ \Rightarrow $$ t $$ \propto $$ $$\sqrt m $$ as ‘q’ is same for electron and proton.

Since, electron has smaller mass so it will take smaller time.
